shortDescription: By Yantoultra NguiTaiwan-based electronic components company WT Microelectronics TWSE:3036 launched a fundraising of up to $940 million through a share sale and a zero-coupon convertible bond issue, according to term sheets reviewed by Reuters on Tuesday.

children: Taiwan-based electronic components company WT Microelectronics
launched a fundraising of up to $940 million through a share sale and a zero-coupon convertible bond issue, according to term sheets reviewed by Reuters on Tuesday.

WT Micro plans to sell 15 million global depositary shares, representing 75 million common shares, for about $440 million. The shares are being offered at $28.84 to $29.46 each, a 5% to 7% discount to the company's closing price on Tuesday.
The company also plans to sell $500 million in zero-coupon convertible bonds due in June 2027. The bonds can be converted into WT Micro shares at a 20% to 25% premium to the share sale price.
WT Micro plans to use the proceeds to buy raw materials priced in foreign currencies and repay foreign-currency bank loans.
The two offerings are being run at the same time but do not depend on each other to close.
WT Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
